title: OIDC Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591 / 7592)
subtitle: A client registers itself with the authorization server over a JSON API, receiving a client_id, optional secret, and management handles — then reads and updates its own record.

steps.label: Build client_metadata
steps.lede: The AS advertises a registration_endpoint in its metadata. The client assembles the client_metadata document it wants: redirect URIs, grant types, response types, and how it will authenticate at the token endpoint.
steps.devtools: DCR is a plain back-channel JSON API — every request and response is directly readable. The interesting part is what metadata you ask for here versus what credentials the AS hands back.

steps.label: POST /register
steps.lede: The client posts the metadata document as JSON. For protected registration it would also send an Authorization: Bearer <initial access token> and/or a signed software_statement JWT in the body.
steps.devtools: Content-Type is application/json. Inspect the body's redirect_uris, grant_types, response_types, and token_endpoint_auth_method. For protected registration, note the Authorization: Bearer header and/or a software_statement JWT inside the JSON.

steps.label: Validate metadata
steps.lede: The AS validates the requested redirect_uris (must be https), grant_types, and scope. For protected registration it also verifies the software_statement's signature against the trusted directory's keys — its claims then override the plain JSON.
steps.devtools: If a software_statement was sent, split it on . and base64url-decode the payload. Its asserted claims (redirect_uris, software_id, token_endpoint_auth_method) override the client-supplied JSON — but only after the AS verifies the signature.

steps.label: 201 Created — credentials + handles
steps.lede: The AS assigns a client_id (and a client_secret for confidential auth methods), plus two management handles: a high-value registration_access_token and the per-client registration_client_uri.
steps.devtools: The response is the most important thing to read. client_secret appears only for confidential auth methods — treat it as a secret. The registration_access_token is a long-lived, high-value bearer credential that can later rewrite redirect_uris — guard it. registration_client_uri is the per-client RFC 7592 management URL.

steps.label: GET registration_client_uri (RFC 7592)
steps.lede: The client reads its own record back, authenticating with the registration_access_token. The AS returns the current metadata.
steps.devtools: The GET carries Authorization: Bearer <registration_access_token>. A PUT to the same URI updates the record (full metadata in the body) and the 200 may return a rotated registration_access_token — if so, the old one is now dead. A DELETE deregisters and returns 204 No Content.

steps.label: Invalid metadata → 400
steps.lede: A registration whose redirect_uri fails policy — here a non-https URI — is rejected. The AS never issues a client for metadata it will not honor.
steps.devtools: A 400 with {"error":"invalid_redirect_uri"} (or invalid_client_metadata) means the AS rejected the requested metadata. On a 7592 management call, a missing / stale / stolen registration_access_token instead returns 401 Unauthorized.
